properties.description: Child component ids in render order. MCP writes it when children are created or reparented; update_components also accepts child names.

renderingHints.childOrder: Children render in the order of properties.childOrder (an array of child component ids); grid top/left of a child are ignored. A child missing from childOrder lands after the listed ones in an arbitrary order. MCP writes childOrder: request order when the container and its children are created together, appended for a child added or reparented later.
renderingHints.childWidth: A child fills the free main-axis width by default (layouts.desktop.fillWidth true). Fill children in a row share the line: equally by default, or by layouts.desktop.grow (grow 2 beside grow 1 takes two thirds). layouts.desktop.minWidthPx is the narrowest a fill child may get; in a row with properties.flexWrap {{true}} a child that would go narrower wraps to the next line (a responsive card grid). For a fixed width set fillWidth=false and widthPx=<pixels>. The grid width/left are still required by the API but do not change the rendered width.
renderingHints.childHeight: A child is its authored layout height in px. Only a child with its own dynamicHeight on grows to its content (in view mode).
renderingHints.containerHeight: With properties.dynamicHeight {{true}} the container grows to fit its children in view mode; the editor keeps the authored height. Without it, children beyond the authored height (padding included) are cut off.
renderingHints.antCard: cardStyle 'antCard' (Ant Design pack, parked: use shadcnCard) draws an Ant Design card: a light surface with an 8px radius and a 1px border, plus a 56px header with cardTitle on the left and cardExtra on the right. The header appears only when cardTitle or cardExtra is set and takes its 56px from the body. In that mode backgroundColor, borderColor and borderRadius styles are ignored.
renderingHints.shadcnCard: cardStyle 'shadcnCard' draws a shadcn/ui card: a light surface with a 14px radius, a 1px border and a faint shadow, plus a header with cardTitle (semibold) and cardExtra as a muted description beneath it. The header takes 48px with a title only and 70px with a description, from the body. Pair it with the Shad* widgets.
renderingHints.spacing: padding and gap are properties in px, not styles.
renderingHints.surface: A FlexContainer is pure layout and is created transparent (no background, no border) unless you give it a surface: cardStyle 'shadcnCard' (a shadcn/ui card with optional cardTitle/cardExtra header) or your own backgroundColor/borderColor. Add a surface only where you want one; rows and columns used for layout stay invisible.

authoringHints.creation: Create the container and its children in one add_components call: the container gets a client_ref, each child the matching parent_ref, listed in display order. Children may share the same top/left (for example 0,0): flex children are not linted for overlap.
authoringHints.reorder: Reorder with update_components on the container: definition.properties.childOrder = [child names or ids] in the wanted order; children left out keep their relative order after the listed ones.
authoringHints.childOrderManaged: Do not author childOrder ids on create; MCP fills them in. A childOrder given on create may name batch children by client_ref or name.

serverSideDataFlow.reactiveReadRule: When page/count options reference Table or external-filter exposed state, prefer runOnDependencyChange=true so reads occur after the new state is published. Keep onPageLoad for initial hydration and onRefresh for explicit refresh.

serverSideDataFlow.eventRule: With reactive reads, onPageChanged/onSearch/onSort/onFilterChanged and external-filter events should not also run those queries. Use them only for non-query effects such as resetting pageIndex to 1; duplicate wiring causes redundant or stale reads.

runtimeCompatibility.rule: For explicit static columns, keep table-level autogenerateColumns=true and useDynamicColumn=false. MCP normalizes these defaults because some ToolJet versions crash while generating column transformations when autogenerateColumns is false.

dataProjection.rule: With explicit columns and autogenerateColumns=true, bind data to a new object containing only visible and behavior-needed keys. A .map(r => r) identity map or {...r} spread is not a projection and can leak undeclared datasource fields.

hiddenDataColumns.rule: When a field is needed by row actions or selectedRow but must not display, keep it in Table data and declare it in columns with columnVisibility=false. This preserves the key while preventing autogenerateColumns from leaking it as a visible column.

inlineEditing.selection: selectedRow and rowData contain the original source row, not the pending inline edits. selectRowOnCellEdit does not change this contract.
inlineEditing.pendingRows: Read pending full rows with Object.values(components.<table>.dataUpdates || {}). dataUpdates and changeSet are objects keyed by row indexes, not database primary keys; updatedData contains all rows with edits merged.
inlineEditing.saveEvent: The native Save changes footer fires onBulkUpdate. Wire a supported mutation to that event before exposing the footer; an editable cell or visible Save control alone does not persist anything.

inlineEditing.validation: Validate edited numbers for finite, nonnegative values before writing; reject negative values, recompute derived status fields from the edited values, and refresh/reset edits only after confirmed success. Verify the saved value after reload.

Per-row styling is data, never a nested binding (a {{ }} inside the columns binding breaks it): conditionalStyles: [{ condition, value, textColor, backgroundColor, fontWeight }] (first match wins; conditions as filters: equals, ne, contains, gt, lt, gte, lte, isEmpty, ...; add key to test another field of the row). A button's disabledWhen / hiddenWhen: { key, condition, value }. Empty columns are generated from the data.
table.selection: allowSelection (single; selectedRow, selectedRowId = data index), showBulkSelector (checkbox column; selectedRows, selectedRowsId), highlightSelectedRow, disableRowDeselection, defaultSelectedRow {key: value}. onRowClicked fires after selectedRow is set; onSelectionChanged on any selection change. Row ids come from idField (default id), so a selection survives a refetch.
table.actions: A button column fires onActionButtonClicked after setting lastActionClicked { buttonId, columnKey, row } and selectedRow to that row: one event handler serves every button, branching on components.<table>.lastActionClicked.buttonId.
table.serverSide: Server-side pagination: serverSidePagination true, data is the current page, bind the query offset to components.<table>.pageIndex (1-based) and rowsPerPage, set totalRecords for page numbers (or toggle enableNextButton), refetch onPageChanged. serverSideSearch / serverSideSort / serverSideFilter stop the table filtering, sorting or searching locally: read searchText, sortApplied [{column, columnKey, direction}] and filters [{column, condition, value}] in the query and refetch on onSearch / onSort / onFilterChanged (each resets pageIndex to 1 except sort). setPage does not fire onPageChanged.
table.editing: isEditable columns edit in place: changeSet {dataIndex: {key: value}}, dataUpdates (full edited rows), updatedData; onCellValueChanged per edit; the Save changes bar fires onBulkUpdate (save there, then refetch: edits clear when the data changes); Discard fires onCancelChanges.
table.chrome: Toolbar: displaySearchBox, showFilterButton, hideColumnSelectorButton (false shows the column chooser), showDownloadButton (CSV/JSON of the filtered, sorted, edited rows), showRefreshButton (onRefresh). cellSize condensed|regular|spacious, tableType regular|striped|bordered, stickyHeader. More than 150 rows on a page are virtualised. Styles: accent, background, header background/text, cell text, secondary text, border, hover, selected, striped, radius, font size, header casing, outer border.

ShadKanban.name: ShadKanban
ShadKanban.description: shadcn/ui Kanban board from data: columns are values of a status field; cards show the fields you map (title, description, badge, tags, progress, meta, avatar), or, with Card content Custom, child components laid out on the card and bound to {{cardData.<field>}}. Drag to move, optional add and delete buttons, and addCard/updateCard/deleteCard/moveCard actions; save changes with queries on the card events (components.<name>.movedCard, lastAddedCard, lastRemovedCard, lastUpdatedCard, cards)

properties.label: Cards

properties.label: Columns (in order)
properties.default: {{[{ id: 'todo', title: 'To do' }, { id: 'doing', title: 'In progress' }, { id: 'done', title: 'Done' }]}}

Column width (px, empty: fill the board)

board.customCards: For card content the fields cannot express (buttons on a card, a custom layout), set cardLayout "custom" and cardHeight (px, the same for every card), then add child components with parent_ref to the board (no slot_name, or "body"). They are laid out on the card canvas: 43 grid columns across the card width (about 7px each on a 3-column board), top in px from the card top. Bind them to {{cardData.<field>}}; every card renders the same children with its own row. A button on a card can act on that card with cardData.id. Children of a board left on Fields content are never shown. Prefer Fields when the mapped fields fit: they need no layout and look right by default.
board.sizing: collapsedHeight (px of card content): taller cards show only that top part with a Show more toggle; put what must always be visible above it (title, owner, status) and details below. Empty shows every card whole; the Show more toggle appears on hover. Columns fold to a narrow strip from a chevron in their header (collapsibleColumns, on by default) and still take dropped cards; collapsedColumns lists column ids folded at start (e.g. a Done or Closed column on a long-running board); components.<name>.collapsedColumns is the current list. columnWidth (px) fixes every column, and the board scrolls sideways when they do not fit; empty shares the board width (at least 240px each).
board.content: A card shows only the fields you map: titleField, descriptionField, badgeField (priority words colour the badge), tagsField (an array or a comma list), progressField (0 to 100), metaField (a short date or count), avatarField (a name, shown as initials). Map what the job needs; leave the rest empty. density "compact" for long boards.
board.saving: Every change shows on the board at once and fires an event with its payload: onCardMoved (movedCard, lastMove), onCardAdded (lastAddedCard), onCardUpdated (lastUpdatedCard), onCardRemoved (lastRemovedCard); components.<name>.cards is the whole board. Save in that event handler with a query. The actions (addCard, updateCard, moveCard, deleteCard) fire the same events, so either call an action and save in its event, or save with a query and refresh the data; never both, or the save runs twice.
board.addFlow: allowAdd shows an Add card button under each column: it sets addCardColumn and fires onAddCardClick. Open a modal form there; on submit run the insert with status components.<name>.addCardColumn, then refresh the data query (or call addCard without a separate insert).
board.deleteFlow: allowDelete shows a delete button on card hover: the card leaves the board and onCardRemoved fires with lastRemovedCard; delete the row in that handler.
board.styles: Every colour falls back to the app theme, so set only what the design needs to blend in: accentColor (selection outline, progress bars, drop line, hover borders); columns: columnBackgroundColor, columnBorderColor, columnBorderRadius (px), columnTitleColor, columnCountBackgroundColor, columnCountTextColor, columnGap (px); cards: cardBackgroundColor, cardBorderColor, cardBorderRadius (px), cardShadow ("none" | "sm" | "md" | "lg", default "sm"), cardTitleColor, cardTextColor (description, meta, progress label), progressColor (progress bars; else the accent). properties.badgeColors maps badge values to colours, e.g. { High: "#dc2626", Low: "#16a34a" } (tinted chip, coloured text); unnamed values keep the built-in colours. Take colours from the app theme or brand, never the defaults of another product.
